links.outcome: Agent success when each skill-library update is validated by a gate versus unvalidated skill writing
links.effect: On MedAgentBench GRASP lifted gpt-oss-120b from 40.6% to 88.8%. Skill writing without validation was no better than using no skills. Adding the same gate to five baselines lifted each in-domain.
links.quote: Ablations attribute the gain to comparative proposal generation, the acceptance gate, and the hard regression budget rather than to skill writing itself, which without validation is no better than using no skills.

unlisted_practices: Gated, regression-budgeted acceptance of self-generated skills into a bounded agent skill library

screen.reason: The paper evaluates an agentic self-improvement method (GRASP) on clinical benchmarks (MedAgentBench, FHIR-based) to improve procedural reliability of LLM agents, representing algorithm/agent architecture development rather than a deployment safeguard.
